articleTitle: New network design for simultaneous use of electric vehicles, photovoltaic generators, wind farms and energy storage
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Renewable energy deployment in a real-time power distribution system is complicated by the unreliability of continuous output. The use of an appropriate mix of the two renewable energy source technologies, PV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>photovoltaic and WT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>wind turbines in conjunction with the usage of an energy storage device, as an example a battery system, as a form of power balancing medium, might address output intermittency and dependability concerns. Different storage methods might help with the unreliability problem, but they consume a lot of electricity and produce a lot of expenses and carbon emissions. As a temporary distributed energy storage device, two-way power transfer capability in plug-in electric cars (V2G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>Vehicle-to-Grid, G2V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>Grid-to- Vehicle) and electric vehicles are an option. In this study, the benefits of two wind and solar resources are compared in a weak low-voltage distribution system, and it is demonstrated that using these two resources together may overcome the problems of generating renewable resources with a stochastic nature. An uneven power distribution, the behavior of the grid at the PCC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>point of common coupling in the presence of a wind turbine, solar generator, and electric vehicle was also studied. Finally, the stability of transients has been investigated under various fault situations. The DIgSILENT PowerFactory program is used to run simulations.

Author Keywords: System integration of wind and solar

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Lithium Battery Management System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The battery is one of the fundamental parts of electric vehicles, mobile phones, laptops, and other electronic equipment. Among all types of rechargeable batteries, lithium-ion batteries are more beneficial because of their appropriate features than other batteries and govern the battery market. In this article, we introduce a Battery Management System for overcoming the electrical and temperature hazards of lithium-ion batteries. The proposed Battery Management System is solely general and manages 10.8V to 48V battery pack at all stages of charge, discharge, and electrical rest, individually. In this way, the battery is protected against over-current when charging and discharging, over-voltage, under-voltage, over-temperature, and under-temperature. The system also has short circuit protection and reverses the connection of the charger protection. The main application and approach of the proposed Battery Management System is electric vehicle battery (48V/50Ah) management. Also, the proposed Battery Management System can work in Master-Slave configuration for high-voltage battery pack management.

articleTitle: Economic Assessment of Residential Hybrid Photovoltaic-Battery Energy Storage System in Iran
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Due to a 15% electricity shortage in Iran, the scheduled shutdown occurs frequently in summer noon in 2021. These power cuts lead to serious social and economic effects on both private and government sectors. As a solution, Mashhad Electric Energy Distribution Company extended the current FiT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>Feed-in-tariff (FiT) framework in a way that any individual can upgrade its existing GCPVS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Grid-connected photovoltaic system (GCPVS) to the hybrid one through exploiting BESS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>Battery energy storage system (BESS) and substituting the grid-tie inverter with a hybrid one. When the grid is present, the investor sells the whole generated energy at a guaranteed price. Further, he/she benefits continuous supply of energy for domestic loads during the grid power cut. This paper presents the economic evaluation of the residential hybrid PV-BESS under FiT policy in Mashhad as a case study. The BESS is initially designed for a traditional residential demand taking the frequency and duration of the power cuts into account. Afterwards, the hybrid system is assessed under the current FiT policy from the economic perspective. The presented analyzes endorse that although the initial cost of the hybrid system raises with respect to the grid-connected type, this project with 463,425,280 Iranian Rials NPV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>Net present value (NPV), 12.68 PBT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>Payback period time (PBT), and 28.3% IRR <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>Internal rate of return (IRR) is economically viable under the current FiT policy.

articleTitle: Strategic Planning for Incorporating Inverter-Based Wind Turbine in Distribution Networks Using Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Incorporating wind turbines (WT) in power systems is increased around the world. Therefore, this paper introduces the optimal allocation of WT with and without enabling inverter in the radial distribution system (RDS). In addition, a recent algorithm called arithmetic optimization algorithm (AOA) is utilized for determining the best sizes and locations for inverter-based WT units in RDS. The system losses are presented as a single objective function taking into accounts the probabilistic of WT output. In this paper, IEEE 69-bus RDS is utilized as a test system. Incorporating WT in RDS enhances the system voltage and decreases system loss. From the results, incorporating multiple WTs give better results than incorporating single WT, and enabling inverter with incorporating WT gives better results than incorporating WT alone in RDS. AOA algorithm proved it is effective to determine the global result as compared to efficient algorithms.

articleTitle: A New Multi-port DC/DC Converter for PV/battery/DC gird Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper proposes a new non-isolated low power Multi-port DC/DC converter for PV/Battery/Load systems. The presented circuit consists of primary converters and can extract maximum power from PV and deliver it to the load port, which is a bipolar DC micro-grid. In addition, the presented circuit can regulate different bipolar output loads on equal voltage levels. In this converter, excessive energy produced by PV is saved in the battery to support the system when PV energy is insufficient for output load. Although the input to output conversion ratio is regulated to make this system suitable for grid voltage levels, the presented circuit can be used in off-grid systems as well. After theoretical analysis, simulation of this system with MatLab/Simulink proves the performance.

articleTitle: Frequency and voltage stability of the microgrid with the penetration of renewable sources
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The microgrid (MG), if properly designed and with an efficient control system, is a platform for the development of distributed and renewable energy-based products. Because MG inertia is low due to its small structure and low resistance to change, it is very difficult to maintain frequency and voltage stability, especially in the island state. Unlike the power grid, inverter-based distributed generation is the main source of MGs. Due to the low response rate of primary energy sources in distributed generation, these productions, even if they have an efficient control system, alone cannot maintain MG stability, so by using electrical energy storage sources and D-STATCOM along with distributed generation, in This research proposes an interactive and multilevel structure for voltage and MG frequency stability. This structure greatly speeds up the MG response to perturbations through an interactive control system. The proposed structure has been implemented and evaluated by MATLAB software on MGs that can be used in both connection and island modes in the presence of a renewable wind source.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of Two High Step-Up DC-DC Converters Applicable in Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The high step-up dc-dc converters are building blocks of PV-based energy systems. These converters provide the voltage-lifting and maximum power point tracking of PVs. The sustainability of such systems depends on reliability of dc-dc converters. This paper investigates the reliability as well as operating life time of two step-up dc-dc converters. Furthermore, the sensitivity of output voltages to the duty cycle has been evaluated. Based on simulation and comparison results, the more reliable converter with longer operating life time has been introduced.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Classification in PV Arrays Using Machine Learning Algorithms in the Presence of Noisy Data
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: With the growth in installed capacity of photovoltaic systems in recent years, fault detection and classification in photovoltaic arrays has become one of the most important topics for improving the efficiency and dependability of these systems. In photovoltaic arrays, due to the non-linear nature, the strong dependence of the output power on the environmental conditions, and the maximum power point tracking presence, fault detection by traditional protection is not possible. As a result, numerous techniques to overcome this limitation have been presented in recent years, one of which is the use of machine learning methods, which have been used more in previous studies. In machine learning techniques, the noise presence can disrupt the algorithm training process. On the other hand, when collecting data from photovoltaic arrays due to human fault or device failure, there may be noise in the data set. For this intent in this paper, we intend to provide a method for fault detection and classification in photovoltaic arrays using machine learning methods with noisy data presence.

articleTitle: A Simple Method for Steady-State Performance Optimization of Doubly-Fed Induction Machines
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Doubly-fed induction machines (DFIMs) are widely used as wind generators. However, these machines can also be used in motor mode as electric propulsion systems in electric vehicles. This paper presents a detailed steady-state analysis of a DFIM. In this study, using the per-phase equivalent circuits and steady-state equations, a comprehensive analysis of the DFIM in motor operation mode is presented. The behavior of the motor in all three synchronous, super-synchronous, and sub-synchronous modes is analyzed and evaluated using the simulation results. Adjusting and controlling the rotor voltage is very essential. Therefore, a simple method for optimally adjusting the amplitude and angle of the rotor voltage is proposed for two different optimization scenarios that maximize output power and efficiency, respectively. According to the results, if the rotor voltage is properly selected, the DFIM can operate optimally at a wide range of speeds.

articleTitle: Effect of fault in output capacitor due to its parasitic resistance in modular DC-DC three-level converter
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, the behavior of a two-module converter after capacitor fault is investigated in this paper. Three-level boost converter in a modular fashion offers multi-input energy sources. This converter with a nonlinear control can control the input power and balance the voltages across the output capacitor. Since aluminum electrolytic capacitors, which have a low lifetime, are usually used in such converters, this paper investigates fault on the output capacitor. The fault is modeled as a parallel resistance, which is high when the capacitor is healthy but low when the capacitor fault. To study the system waveforms, two cases are considered. A high value to show the normal mode and a small value to show the fault mode for the fault resistance are set. MATLAB/Simulink software is used to perform the modeling and validate the hypothesis. The voltage balance and the regulation of the DC bus voltage are studied for these two scenarios.

articleTitle: Determination of online DATC with uncertainty and state estimation
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The present paper, firstly, reviews the static and dynamic ATC (SATC-DATC) determination methods. Secondly, it investigates the state estimate online mode. In this paper, the static ENRS-DR+ method, which combines the NRS method with DH and corrects both methods, is employed. EPEBS and EPOMP have also been used in combination to determine transient stability that is, any correction to previous methods. A combination of online state estimation, transient stability, and static method led to a combined approach for DATC (CDATC). The results on a large and real network show its suitability, speed, and higher accuracy than the FADATC method. The ideas are demonstrated on Iowa State (145 bus) and the east of Iran (849 bus) networks.

articleTitle: Modeling, simulation, and parameters identification of a lithium-ion battery used in electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Batteries are the most important part of every Electric Vehicle(EV) and have an underlying role that is supplying power to all parts of the vehicle. Among different kinds of batteries, the lithium-ion family is considerably used in several industries. The electrical model of the battery gets remarkable attention and, numerous equivalent circuits have been proposed in recent years since the parameters of the batteries are not available in their datasheets. The main goal of this paper is to estimate the parameters of a second-order RC equivalent circuit of a 2600mah lithium-ion battery which can be used for different purposes. Besides, the parameters of a first-order RC equivalent circuit are identified in advance to make a comparison between the results of the two models. For this purpose, some standard tests are performed multiple times in the laboratory to achieve the best results. Afterward, these models are simulated in Simulink/Matlab environment in order to verify the output precision of these models by using the real data at 25°C. It is concluded that the second-order circuit is more efficient and precise than the first-order one and, the amount of three different errors of the second-order circuit is less than those of the first-order one. It should be noted that in this article the hysteresis and temperature effects on the battery are neglected.

articleTitle: Control of Standalone Single-Stage Photovoltaic Pumping System Using State Feedback Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Renewable energy can decrease environmental problems. A photovoltaic pumping system is an easy and effective method to pump the water for remote areas and irrigation demands. The photovoltaic module's maximum power point tracking can be tracked by switching the power converter. This paper proposes a linear quadratic regulator-based state feedback control approach to control a standalone single-stage photovoltaic pumping system with a permanent magnet synchronous motor. Using a solar photovoltaic array, this topology converts solar energy into electrical energy while extracting maximum power from the solar photovoltaic array. Converted electrical energy is delivered to permanent magnet synchronous motor drive by voltage source inverter. The permanent magnet synchronous motor rotates the water pump mechanically coupled to the permanent magnet synchronous motor through a shaft. Through MATLAB/Simulink environment, the photovoltaic pumping system is modeled and simulated. Steady-state and starting behaviors and the photovoltaic pumping system's dynamic performance are evaluated in different conditions by changes in solar irradiance. The comprehensive harmonic distortion analysis of stator currents shows that the suggested control offers low total harmonic distortion.

articleTitle: Long-Term Wind Speed and Power Forecasting Based on LSTM: A Comprehensive Study
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: One of the aspects of sustainable development is attaining grid operation safety management at the right quality level. Since wind energy is also based on renewable energy, its development and improvement are in line with sustainable development goals. However, there are challenges to managing this energy that needs to be addressed. Considering the behavior of wind speed and power of turbines are two effective issues in controlling wind power since lack of this awareness leads to a decline in the quality of customer service or energy waste. Predicting these two factors is one of the fundamental issues in the design and operation of power generation and distribution systems. In this paper, the wind speed and wind power of wind turbines are predicted based on the combined model AM CNN Bi-LSTM. To show the performance of this model, the results of their accuracy and prediction error are compared with the results of LSTM and CNN-LSTM. In all datasets, the results of the proposed model were more successful than other current models, and in the best case, an accuracy of 98.17% was obtained for power forecasting.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of DC Fault Current Limiters for DC Renewable Energy Generators
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: As DC renewable energy generators extensive development in the recent years, the need for applicable protection methods has vitally increased. Solar panels, wind turbines, combined heat and power, and solar thermal panels are all vulnerable power generators in DC renewable energy which necessarily need to be preserved from DC fault current. However, DC renewable energy are difficult to control and protect in the fault case even though they are easy to use in the normal state. Short circuits and Potential risks are controlled with protective equipment based on fault current. There is a fundamental role for fault current limiters (FCL) in creating these disparities. In this paper, DC FCLs as vital equipment to protect DC renewable energy will reviewed and than a comprehensive summary of the limiters are presented and compared.

articleTitle: Optimal Energy Management in Smart Home Considering Renewable Energies, Electric Vehicle, and Demand-Side Management
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, a home energy management system has been designed for a smart home using renewable energy sources. In fact, the optimization of the system is done in the form of seven scenarios in the presence of photovoltaic (PV) system, wind system, battery energy storage system, battery electric vehicle (BEV), and demand-side management (DSM). To implement DSM, various types of incentive-based and time-based demand response (DR) programs with exponential and logarithmic models have been considered. The beta and Weibull probability density functions (PDF) have been used to model the uncertainty of solar irradiance and wind speed. To generate scenarios of solar irradiance and wind speed, the Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) method is used. Also, to reduce the number of generated scenarios, the K-mean clustering algorithm is used. A grid-connected home in Australia is chosen as a case study. At the end of the study, the simulation results are explained, the effects of DR programs on the energy cost of homeowner are discussed.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Differential Scaling Method for Islanding Detection in a PV system
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In recent years, the implementation of renewable energy sources has been growth dramatically due to their numerous advantages. Among different renewable resources, the Photovoltaic (PV) system is one of the most renowned renewable sources due to existence of a great amount of solar radiations that eases expansion of PV systems. Notwithstanding, several types of faults, undesirable islanding, etc., have involved PV systems in great challenges. In this paper, a real-time differential scaling method is developed to detect the islanding events in PV systems. In the proposed approach, only the voltage signal of PV arrays is used. The method is based on monitoring the changes in the voltage of PV array and using it as an indicator of islanding. Thus, if the monitored values exceed a pre-determined threshold, occurrence of an islanding situation in the system will be indicated. The proposed algorithm is not relied on complex signal processing techniques, making it advantageous due to low computational burden for extraction of desired features. The performance of the method is assessed by simulating a typical system in MATLAB/Simulink, and the validity of it is verified.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling and Electrical Equivalent Circuit Extraction for a Flux Switching PM Motor for EVs
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Flux switching permanent magnet motor (FSPMM) is a competitive candidate for high torque density and high-speed capability applications. Due to the high non-linear structure, generally, finite element analysis (FEA) is applied to the motor structure to calculate the electromagnetic performance of the FSPMM. The time-consuming behavior of this method leads to the search for new techniques. Magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) and Fourier series analysis (FSA) have been adopted to the FSPMM. However, the former suffers from coarse discretization, and the latter contains complicated mathematical structures. In this paper, the machine equations in the ABC-reference frame and DQ-frame will be extracted, and the electromagnetic performance of a 12/10 FSPMM is evaluated using the electrical equivalent circuit (EEC). The inductance matrix of the machine is the base of this model. Therefore, the method can be used in the other structures of the FSPMM, such as the axial one or the radial with a different number of poles and slots. To verify the correctness of the proposed method, we compare the results. The simulation results, such as electromagnetic torque, self-inductance, mutual inductance, input power, and efficiency of the proposed method, align well with FEA results.

articleTitle: A Quadratic DC-DC converter with Continuous Input Current And Selectable Duty Cycle to Provide A Zero Current Switching of Switch Suitable for renewable Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, a quadratic DC-DC converter has been proposed. Besides the increase of the voltage gain, the continuous input current has been provided. Moreover, it has been designed in a way that can experience zero current switching by a percentage of the duty cycle. Furthermore, it has been tried to increase the voltage gain by 2 inductors to keep the volume as low as possible. The appropriate analysis has been done in both the ideal and non-ideal modes. Additionally, the small-signal analysis has been done in the ideal mode by Matlab. Finally, the simulation outcomes have been extracted and compared with the theoretical relations and considerations. The employed software was PLECS in this study.

articleTitle: A Double-Gain 5-Level Grid-Connected DC-AC Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper suggests a high-efficiency switched-capacitor based transformer-less 5-level grid-tied inverter that operates based on series-parallel charge/discharge of capacitor-cells. The structure is capable of limiting the capacitors' impulsive charging current. This structure employs the Peak Current Control (PCC) technique to generate the switching pulses, and control the active/reactive power flow by properly controlling the injected current into the grid. The leakage-current issue is resolved, due to presence of Common-Ground-Point (CGP). This feature along with the ability of working in both buck or boost modes, makes the suggested converter suitable for PV-applications. The multi-step waveform leads to less-THD, and compact filter-size. The correct function of suggested converter has been affirmed by simulation results, for a 520W prototype.

articleTitle: The Survey of Commercialized HVDC Circuit Breakers Main Features for Off Shore Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Wind energy is the most useful type of renewable energy and wind farms are also expanding following the development of renewable energy and energy marketing. One of the types of wind farms used in the world are offshore wind farms with a length of more than 200 km, which use HVDC lines. the key concern of the offshore wind farms extensive implementation is its sensitivity in the short circuit faults. Increasing the short-circuit level and fast raising nature of the DC fault currents are some reasons for importance of protection system and choosing the appropriate protection component that is critical issue for development of offshore wind farms. Breakers are one of the main components of protection and therefore choosing a suitable breaker is vital. Breaker main features in various types of DCCB is different based on its topology characteristic. This paper aim to survey breaker main features in types of DCCBs.

articleTitle: A Fast Holomorphic Method to Evaluate Available Transmission Capacity with Large Scale Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, to take advantage of the two methods, Holomorphic embedding power or load flow and Newton Raphson, both were combined. In an attempt to rectify earlier techniques, a potential energy barrier surface estimate was also used in conjunction to assess transient stability. A hybrid technique for dynamic available transfer capacity computation was developed using a combination of dynamic and static methods. In a large, real-world network, the findings showed greater appropriateness, accuracy, and speed than existing dynamic available transfer capacity techniques. This was proven in the west of Iran (848 buses) where there are several wind farms.

articleTitle: Stochastic multi-objective optimization with the aim of household energy management
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Currently, the use of renewable energy is considered to assist in meeting the demand for energy in residential homes. Utilization of renewable energy causes greenhouse gas emissions reduction. In this regard, a multi-objective two-stage scenario-based stochastic optimization is proposed in this paper. Uncertainties related to solar radiation and electrical load are assumed based on their specific probabilistic distribution function (PDF). To generate a large number of scenarios with the aim of modeling the uncertainties in this problem, the Monte-Carlo method is employed. Then, a comprehensive clustering method for scenario reduction is proposed. The residential energy hub has also considered integrating fuel cell and natural gas resources to supply thermal and electrical demands. Minimizing energy supply costs in a residential home is considered to be simultaneous with minimizing greenhouse gas emissions. A Pareto front including non-dominated solutions is then used to show the optimal points. A sensitivity analysis is also performed on the battery capacity to investigate its effect on electrical and thermal results. Therefore, an appropriate battery capacity according to stochastic multi-objective optimization can be specified.

articleTitle: Comparison behavior of the capacitor voltages balancing using linear and nonlinear controllers
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: One common way to evaluate the performance of a controller is to compare it with the classical controllers. In this paper, the behavior of a nonlinear controller for the two-module converter is compared with the classic PI controller. This converter is used to neutralize the issue of DC voltage imbalance. The comparison between an indirect sliding mode controller and a PI controller is completed. It is performed in two scenarios: in the first scenario, comparing the performance of the two controllers in the DC balancing of the capacitor voltages and in the second scenario, the dynamics of the input powers for photovoltaic and fuel cell application. To ensure the optimal PI performance, the control parameters are determined using an average linearized model of the system. To perform the modeling and the comparison, MATLAB/Simulink software is used. The simulation results verify that balancing of the capacitor voltage during the transient regime and the steady-state regime for both controllers.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Active Distribution Network Flexibility to Energy Storage System Capacity
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Although renewable energy penetration creates environmental and economic advantages for the network, it initiates challenges to the distribution network flexibility because of its uncertainty. Taking benefit of different flexibility sources to decrease or even remove the renewable energy fluctuation effects is an important factor in the operation of future distribution systems. Constructing a highly consistent flexibility assessment technique is a crucial issue. In the paper, a flexibility assessment method is presented which is based on the feasibility evaluation of the uncertain zone of renewable energy resources generation and load. In addition, the sensitivity of flexibility to the energy storage system capacity is inspected. In order to confirm the performance of proposed model, it is tested on the IEEE 33-bus radial distribution system. The outcomes of simulation demonstrate the effect storage system on the improvement of distribution network flexibility. Moreover, the sensitivity study outcomes can reveal the appropriate capacity of storage facility for the secure operation of distribution network.

articleTitle: Enhancing passive solar heating in zero energy buildings using PCMs: Economic investigation of a Hotel in Mashhad, Iran
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Nowadays, due to lack of energy resources, rising prices of energy carriers the need to optimize energy consumption, therefore moving towards the green buildings is felt more. Energy consumption in Iran is 2.5 times the global average. According to the energy balance sheet in Iran, about 41% of energy consumption in this country is related to the construction sector, due to non-compliance with construction principles and also not using appropriate and optimal materials. One of the suitable solutions for optimal energy building construction is the use of phase change materials (PCM) as a new insulation coating on the outer walls of the building. These materials can be used as a source of heat energy storage due to their high latent heat property. In this study, by simulating a hotel in Mashhad, using Design Builder software, the effect of using phase change materials as a source of inactivated solar heating in the building is investigated. Obviously, the use of these materials requires initial costs and investments, which varies depending on the type, amount and properties of the selected materials. Eventually, economic indicators are extracted by analyzing the costs and benefits of saving energy for the selected building. It was found that the use of these materials in large buildings such as hotels would have relatively high initial cost, but since at best it reduces energy consumption by about 6%, this cost will be compensated in the long run.

articleTitle: A two-stage grid-connected single-phase micro-inverter with long lifetime, continuous input current and fewer number of switches
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper proposes a grid-connected single-phase MI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>micro-inverter with a rated power of 300 W and an appropriate control strategy for PV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>photovoltaic systems. The proposed MI is designed based on a two-stage topology. The first stage consists of a SEPIC DC-DC converter with high voltage gain, while the second stage includes a full-bridge DC-AC converter. The high voltage gain is obtained in the first stage of the proposed MI by adjusting the coupled inductor conversion ratio at the low duty cycle ratio of the switch. The advantages of the proposed MI are the use of fewer components to provide suitable output voltage level for connection to a single-phase network, continuous input current, limited voltage stress on the switch, long operational lifetime, and high reliability. Lower input current ripple and the presence of film capacitors in the power decoupling circuit increase the lifetime and reliability of the proposed MI. The continuous input current in the proposed MI helps to the MPPT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>maximum power point tracking in PV panel with an efficiency of %99. The operating principles of the proposed MI are analyzed under different conditions. The results of design and simulation confirm the advantages and proper performance of the proposed MI.

articleTitle: Real-Time Inertia Estimation of Power System with High Penetration of Renewables
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Nowadays, according to the high penetration of renewable energy sources, the importance of inertia estimation has become more critical than ever. Renewables cause uncertainty and stochasticity and reduce the total inertia of the power system. Therefore, transmission system operators in a changing environment are going to face transient instability increasingly. Thus, a fast and accurate technique for real-time estimation is required. It allows the operator to monitor the system immediately and make an appropriate decision. This paper proposes a real-time inertia estimation method based on the swing equation for a multi-area interconnected power system using the Phasor Measurement Units. The proposed approach's efficiency is validated through time-domain simulation on the two-area four-generator test power system. The numerical results demonstrate the potential and precision of the proposed approach in estimating inertia and confirming the modeling assumptions.

articleTitle: A Modified Three-Phase LLC Resonant Converter: Phase Shedding and Light-Load Operation Suitable for Welding Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Recently, three-phase LLC resonant converters have gained attention due to their appealing features, particularly in medium to high power level applications. A modified three-phase LLC converter has been proposed in this paper, which is able to perform in four different operating modes. Among its unique features, the converter, in addition to its sound three-phase operation, provides two-phase operating mode by phase shedding strategy, providing limited output current ripple. Moreover, the proposed converter light load operation can be improved through given full-bridge structure, supplying relatively high output voltage in standby condition as well. Including its benefits, the proposed converter is well-suited for welding applications in which power saving along with welding performance are of paramount importance. To explain the proposed converter's operating modes, simulation results through MATLAB-Simulink are given of a 2 kW/20V case study.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Feasibility Analysis of Enhancing Photovoltaic Lighting Systems with Intelligent Controllers
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Applying clean and renewable energy fed devices and technologies changed into a vital necessity in the world. PV lighting systems are one of the most well-known applications of renewable energies, in cities and public places. However, short life span of battery in conventional PV lighting systems is a main drawback. Promoting these systems to IoT intelligent charge controller implies many technical advantages, including programmable lighting profile during night and supplying illumination until morning, lengthening device life span, especially batteries, decrease extra CapEx for establishing central emergency lighting system. In this paper, techno-economic analysis of promoting 122 light poles in a public park in Mashhad is performed. Results showed that economical indices prove the profitability of the project, with 63.7 % IRR, 3.15-year payback period and 85.3 million Rial NPV.

articleTitle: Reconfiguration of Zafarana Stage-l Wind Farm Layout Based on Marine Predators Algorithm Considering Wake Effect
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In the last years, the importance of wind farms layout has appeared on the surface. The simple definition of optimal layout is how to extract the maximum power from the wind at certain area with lower cost. The wind speed in the wind farm site will be affected by the distribution of wind turbines in this site. The lack of optimal distribution of wind turbines will lead to wake effect. This wake effect will reduce the output power of wind farms. From this point, this paper uses Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA) to redistribute the wind turbines of Zafarana Stage-1 Wind Farm (Zafarana-1). The proposed layout based on MPA takes into consideration the parameters of wind turbines which are already used in Zafarana-1. The proposed layout based on MPA is designed to increase the efficiency of Zafarana-1 considering wake effect. The proposed layout based on MPA can enhance the output power of Zafarana-1 at less area than the currently allocated area of Zafarana-1.

articleTitle: A Single-Switch, Coupled Inductor Based Quadratic High Step-Up DC-DC Converter with Low Switch Voltage Stress
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, a single-switch, coupled inductor based quadratic high step-up dc-dc converter with low switch voltage stress and continuous input current converter is introduced. The proposed converter utilizes coupled inductors in its topology which contributes to high conversion ratio. Only one switch is implemented in the proposed converter and a passive clamp circuit is used in order to decrease switching losses and increase efficiency. The input current of the proposed converter is continuous and this makes it a suitable candidate for renewable energy applications such as photovoltaics and fuel cells since continuous input current contributes to small input filters. The operation principles of the proposed converter are discussed, and simulations have been carried out in order to validate the operation of the converter. Moreover, the introduced converter is compared to other similar topologies in different basis such as voltage gain, efficiency, number of components and voltage stress on switch.

articleTitle: A Review of Emerging Cutting-Edge Energy Storage Technologies for Smart Grids Purposes
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: With the increase in the use of hybrid and renewable energy sources within the scope of measures taken to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the difficulties brought by daily and seasonal changes in transmission and distribution need to be tackled. Energy storage systems (ESS) are essential technologies because of the support they provide in times of need to overcome supply-demand balance challenges. For this reason, worldwide efforts are being made to develop more efficient energy storage systems. Energy storage facilities can be employed for various purposes in power systems such as reliability procurement, frequency regulation, or redressing fluctuation caused by uncertain and intermittent sources. These technologies deliver power in various scales and various response speed. Even though pumped storage technology is the most common type of grid-scale energy storage, various on-going studies are still looking for other efficient alternatives. Some emerging large-scale storage technologies have been proposed, or even tested as a prototype in small scale. The suggested paradigm needs to be further matured in terms of efficiency and investment cost. This article aims to examine worldwide energy storage applications, their location, applied energy storage technology, total energy and power capacity, and power quality issues.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Assessment of Wind Turbine Impact on Distribution Networks by Using Latin Hypercube Sampling Method
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Determining the appropriate location for distributed generation resources to gain the maximum benefits is still a very challenging problem. Most of the losses in power networks happen in the distribution part. Distributed generation units, if placed in appropriate places, in addition to supplying the demand, could help reduce losses and improve voltage profile considerably. In this paper, the optimal placement of wind turbines for improving voltage profile and decreasing losses has been carried out. Since the voltage of the network buses and its losses depends on system load and installed distributed generation resources, it is necessary to determine the status of the distribution system at first then evaluation is done. A wind turbine will have different generation values depending on the speed of the wind that varies in different hours of a year. So, it is necessary to perform optimal placement for obtaining the optimum solution (improving voltage profile and reducing losses) considering the uncertainty of two variables, wind turbine generation, and network load by probabilistic assessment. In this paper, for reducing calculation and keeping the desired accuracy, the Latin Hypercube Sampling has been used. Also, there is a correlation between wind turbine generation and network load variables. Taking this correlation into account will make the simulations more realistic that is realized by the Cholesky decomposition method.

articleTitle: Optimal Energy Management of a Smart Building Considering Rooftop Photovoltaic, Electric Vehicles and Schedulable Loads
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for energy management of a smart building including photovoltaic (PV) system, battery energy storage (BES), electric vehicles (EVs) and different load types. Indeed, using the developed model, the optimal cost day ahead energy scheduling of all types of loads which can participate in demand response program and charge/discharge regime of electric vehicle and battery energy storage system are determined. The studied system can interact with the power grid for both buy or sell electricity. Eventually, the main goal of the optimization problem is minimizing the customer costs considering EV and BESS depreciation. The whole problem including objective function and operational constraints are formulated as a mixed integer linear program (MILP) model and solved by CPLEX method using GAMS software. A real smart building located in Tehran, Iran is utilized as the study case and the efficiency and applicability of the proposed household energy management method is evaluated using real data for a summer, winter and rainy day.

articleTitle: A review of new flare gases recovery methods to increase energy efficiency and reduce pollutants
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In addition to wasting energy, burning flare gases is a threat to the environment and the world. Among the leading producers of greenhouse gases are refineries, oil and gas production units, and thermal power plants, which emit large amounts of toxic gases into the Earth's atmosphere by burning fossil fuels. Among the ways to control greenhouse gases from the perspective of primary energy sources are to reduce the use of fossil fuels and use alternative primary energy sources such as wind, solar, optimizing energy consumption by improving energy production efficiency and reducing energy lost in various energy systems. Flare gases worldwide are burned or collected, the collection methods and purposes of which are different for each country. Flare gases collection methods include transportation lines, electricity generation, natural gas liquefaction, gas liquefaction, collection and injection to increase oil and gas recovery, and combined methods. In this article, a review of the optimal techniques for recovering flare gases energy, classification and transformation of this threat into an opportunity in Iran and the world that have been studied by researchers and methods for recovering energy from flare gases and preventing the burning of these gases from using them have been presented.

articleTitle: MCDM for renewable energy projects: criteria weighting with traditional entropy and novel hierarchy in combination with conventional and structured in blocks AHP approaches
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Word economies face 2 interlinked and challenging environmental issues - climate control and dependence on traditional hydrocarbon energy sources The development of Renewable Energy (RE) technologies has to ensure the balance of several conflicting objectives with different factors. This paper examines the integration of traditional and novel methods for a subjective and objective definition of the weights of criteria for assessing RE investment projects and their modelling according to the different preferences of users and Decision Makers (DMs).

articleTitle: A Linear Model for Wind Farms Preventive Maintenance Scheduling Considering the Wind Speed Uncertainty and Electricity Market Conditions
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The increasing installation of wind farms in different countries has raised the importance of their reliability and availability. A basic solution for this issue is preventive maintenance, in which the shutdown arrangement of the turbines is scheduled so that the required power is provided without interruption. In this regard, two important goals must be considered simultaneously. First, maximizing the profits, and second, maintaining the reliability to an acceptable level. In this paper, a linear model is proposed for the wind farm preventive maintenance schedule which maximizes the wind farm profit and considers various constraints including reliability threshold, supply and demand, maintenance necessity, continuity, and duration, the allowable number of turbines in maintenance, priority and deadline, manpower and cranes availability, and so on. In the proposed model, the market price of electricity is included in the calculation of farm income, and some constraints are proposed for the first time. In addition, the uncertainty of wind farm generation is considered based on the Weibull wind speed distribution function and deterministic equivalencing method. The proposed linear model for preventive maintenance scheduling has been implemented on a wind farm with 50 units over a 52-week time horizon, and the results show that the power plant profit is maximized and the reliability is also maintained to an acceptable level.

articleTitle: A Stochastic Day-ahead Energy Management under Fault Occurrence Conditions in Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel stochastic energy management scheme that utilizes UC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>Unit Commitment in a concurrent manner with reconfiguration to achieve optimal day-ahead scheduling of MGs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Mico-Grids. The uncertain variables that the problem deals with are load demand, WT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>wind turbine generation, the hour at which line outage starts, and the outage duration. Indeed, the proposed algorithm is intended to maximize the OF<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>Objective Function, i.e. MG's day-ahead profit. Therefore, the optimal set points of the MG's units, the amount of battery charge or discharge, the amount of exchanging power with the connected grid and the best topology of the MG for day-ahead power market are determined under condition of outage of one distribution line. The PSO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm is applied as the solver and a simple approach is defined to adopt the MGs' topology in reconfiguration problems. Moreover, the loads are divided into vital and not-vital loads, and a load-shedding program is utilized in islanding mode. To model the uncertainties, a number of scenarios are created based on MCS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>Monte Carlo Simulation, and MG optimal operation in conditions of fault occurrence is analyzed under these scenarios. Finally, scenario aggregation method is utilized to estimate the MG's day ahead profit under diverse line fault conditions, which makes it possible for MG owner to reduce the undesirable effect of uncertainties on its profit by generating various scenarios. A 10-bus MG consisting of wind turbine, battery, MTs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>Micro-Turbines, vital and non-vital loads is considered as case study.

articleTitle: A Novel Frequency and Voltage Control Method for Islanded Micro-grid
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Two performance modes, connected to grid and grid independent, can be considered for microgrids. In connected mode, the grid voltage and frequency are controlled by the grid and the microgrid controls the exchange of electrical power with the grid. In a standalone mode where there is no connection between the microgrid and the main grid, the microgrid is responsible for regulating voltage and frequency. One of the critical issues of microgrids, in a separate state from the power system, is frequency and voltage control. In this paper, the improvement of microgrid control performance in the field of voltage and frequency is investigated. voltage and frequency control are investigated to improve the performance of the micro-grid. Different types of distributed generation (DG) have been used to investigate and improve voltage stability. A new combination of teaching-learning based optimization (TLBO) and harmonic search algorithm (HSA) has been used for optimal performance in islanded Microgrid. Performance optimization is accomplished by finding the optimal parameters for the droop coefficient of the distributed generation resources and the reliability of the wind units in order to reduce the cost of generated energy. Optimization is defined as a multi-objective problem, and the objective functions are used to minimize fuel consumption of distributed generation and improve the voltage characteristic and microgrid stability of operating and protection constraints. System steady state frequency, reference frequency, droop coefficients and reference voltage of the distributed generation unit are considered as optimization variables. The proposed method is compared with other methods for the 33-bus microgrid using MATLAB software. The simulation results show that the proposed method improves the performance of the microgrid

articleTitle: A New Experimental MPPT and Speed Control Method for 5 kW Stand-Alone Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Nowadays, renewable energy suppliers, specifically small-scale off-grid wind turbines, play a vital role in electricity supplement for outland regions. Since there are some limitations in the generator power, controlling the generator speed is almost a challenge in off-grid applications. In such applications, the user decides when to turn on/ off the electrical load. When the wind speed and the mechanical energy production rate are high while the consumption of electrical charge is low, controlling and stabilizing the generator will be challenging. In addition, due to the stochastic nature of the energy source (wind), the turbine should keep the battery bank full to avoid unwanted outages. In this article, we demonstrate the electrical details and the control system of a stand- alone 5 kW wind turbine designed and manufactured at the Sun-Air Research Institute. Various control scenarios are investigated and applied to the simulation file. Finally, the results of the physical simulator and Simulink in MATLAB are compared and analyzed.

articleTitle: Frequency and Voltage Rapid Restoration in Networked Microgrids with Model Predictive Controller
publicationTitle: 2022 9th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The production of electricity and its transmission has a long history, but with the increase in demand and electricity supply to different areas and the prevention of environmental pollution in recent decades, the use of renewable energy sources has received much attention. Microgrids are used to harness renewable energy and are connected to the main power grid, but when a fault occurs in the power system, the microgrids are disconnected from the main grid according to IEEE1547. After debugging by FERC2222, all microgrids must be reconnected to the main grid, but there is a condition for this: all microgrids must have the same frequency and voltage as the reference values. This study, by designing a predictive controller, quickly recovers frequency and voltage, even in the presence of uncertainty. This paper also presents a large signal model for the microgrid. The microgrid model and the predictive controller are simulated in the MATLAB / Simulink environment, and the controller is proven to recover frequency and voltage in the presence of uncertainties such as overload, change of LC filter parameters, and change of DG connections.
